title: Flag unchanged planned files before verification starts
summary: Add a pre-verification check in the producer loop (crates/athena-core/src/run/mod.rs): compare the candidate's change list with the accepted job plan's files (create/modify/delete) and the reading's deliverables. Each one left unchanged is sent back with the criteria send-back, or the producer's report must say why. If it is still unexplained, the gap is flagged for the verifier. Include a test that a candidate missing a planned file is flagged. Audience: Athena maintainers and the verifier, who found these gaps late.

defaults_applied.how: New tests for the check; cargo test and clippy must pass.
Criteria check a candidate with a missing planned file being flagged, not that code exists.
Fixes the producer hand-in gap, not just the two named jobs.
One focused change to the producer self-check.
Behavior criteria name cargo test commands the verifier can run.
The check is the flag on a missing planned file, not the activity of comparing.
Doc comments and changelog written for an outside reader.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The mechanism extends the existing self-check and send-back (unmet_criteria, send_back_text, PRODUCER_SEND_BACKS): it runs on the producer's report and the snapshot change list before the candidate is built, and shares the one send-back rather than adding a second.

Planned files come from the accepted JobPlan.files, and expected deliverables from the accepted reading's deliverables. A planned file counts as changed when its path is in the snapshot's change list. Deleted planned files count when the action is delete.

Producer output may need an optional field (for example unchanged_planned_files with a reason per path) so a justification can be machine-checked; if the schema already has a suitable field, reuse it.
The check is a flag and send-back, not a hard failure: after the send-back the gap goes to the verifier, matching how unmet criteria are handled today.
Jobs without planning have only the reading's deliverables to compare. The missed time target (performance-target-criterion-set-without-measured-feasibility) is out of scope.

acceptance_criteria.text: A new unit test builds a candidate change list that omits one planned file (for example a crates/athena-cli/tests path in the plan's files) and asserts the check returns that path as flagged; run with cargo test -p athena-core.
A new test shows a candidate that changes every planned file, or whose report gives a reason for an unchanged one, is not flagged; run with cargo test -p athena-core.

A test of the producer loop shows an unexplained missing planned file triggers the send-back text naming the path, and that after the send-back the gap is recorded for the verifier rather than silently passing; run with cargo test -p athena-core.
The check runs in the producer step before verification starts, and the send-back brief and the producer prompt state that planned files left unchanged must be changed or explained in the report.
The missed time target is not touched; the change only concerns unchanged planned files and deliverables.
cargo test, cargo clippy and cargo fmt --check pass for the workspace.

out_of_scope: Changing the verifier's own judgment or findings logic.
Editing athena.toml, defaults.toml or workflow files.
departures: Cost and time sit above the reference because the change touches the central producer loop and needs tests with fake agents.
urgent_reason: Cuts rejected attempts and redo-work retries: it catches a missing planned file before the verifier does, rather than after.
hard_reason: Changes the producer-to-verifier hand-in gate in run/mod.rs, which affects which candidates reach verification and landing.
